record.paper_title: D-symmetric operators: comments and some open problems
record.original_question: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let L(H) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on H, and call an operator A in L(H) D-symmetric when the norm closure of the range of the inner derivation δ_A(X)=AX-XA is equal to the norm closure of the range of δ_{A*}. If A and B are D-symmetric operators on H, under what conditions is their direct sum A⊕B also a D-symmetric operator?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.1. An operator A ∈ L(H) is called D-symmetric, if R(δA) = R(δA∗ ).
Question. Under what conditions the direct sum of two D-symmetric operators is a D-symmetric operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let L(H) denote the C*-algebra of bounded linear operators on H. For an operator A ∈ L(H), define the inner derivation δ_A : L(H) → L(H) by δ_A(X) = AX − XA, and let R(δ_A) denote its range. Call an operator A ∈ L(H) D-symmetric if the norm closures of the ranges of δ_A and δ_{A*} coincide, i.e.

    closure(R(δ_A)) = closure(R(δ_{A*})).

Given two D-symmetric operators A, B ∈ L(H), determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which their direct sum A ⊕ B, viewed as a bounded linear operator on H ⊕ H, is again D-symmetric.
artifact.status_search_result: D-symmetric operators have been studied since the 1970s (e.g., Anderson–Foiaş, Williams), and partial results exist on when the class is closed under direct sums (e.g., when one summand is normal or has special spectral properties). A general necessary-and-sufficient characterization of when the direct sum of two D-symmetric operators is D-symmetric does not appear in the literature, and the question is repeatedly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.claim: D-symmetric operators are an actively studied class but a general direct-sum characterization is not given.

status_evidence.title: On self-adjoint derivation ranges (Pacific J. Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of compact D-symmetric operators are obtained; the general structure problem remains.
status_evidence.claim: The literature provides partial structural results but leaves the direct-sum question unresolved.
